meta.jhaNotes:
BE Survey Notes: Dover AFB high-risk workplace (20 personnel) maintaining roads and flightlines.
Measured Noise (98.6 dBA) and Silica (Quartz/Total Respirable: ~0.28 mg/m3) exposures are significantly above OEL.
JHA Findings & Major Hazards: Hazardous noise from heavy equipment, pneumatic tools, and flightline operations; respirable crystalline silica during demolition/cutting operations; Methanol skin absorption during weekly vehicle disassembly.
Controls: Double hearing protection (plugs and muffs); 3M 7800S respirators; chemical splash goggles; mandatory administrative training (silica, respiratory protection, heat/cold stress, hearing conservation).
Special Restrictions: Fetal Protection Program requires pregnant personnel to report immediately to Public Health for workplace evaluations, restriction recommendations (AF Form 422), and briefings.
Shop supervisors not requiring exams have a 0.00 dBA Noise E

Ambulance & Emergency Response (Life, Limb, or Eyesight)

Immediately Call: Dial 911 (or 302-677-3333 if calling from a cellular device on base)
On-Base Response: Emergency medical dispatch coordinates through the Dover AFB Emergency Communication Center. On base, emergency medical response is provided 24/7 by the Ambulance Response Team (ART) (436th Medical Group / Civil Engineer Squadron Fire Station) in coordination with local Kent County/City of Dover EMS.

Actions On Scene:
State your exact building number (e.g., Bldg 626 / Power Production Shop), specific shop area/bay, and nature of injury.
Direct someone to flag down the emergency vehicle at the hangar/bay apron or street entrance.
For chemical contamination (e.g., methanol, solvent splashes, silica in eyes), begin immediate flushing at the eyewash station/drench shower and inform dispatch of the chemical involved.

Hospital & Emergency Room (Off-Base)

The 436th Medical Group Clinic on base does NOT have an Emergency Room. For severe trauma, life-threatening injuries, or after-hours emergencies requiring hospital care:

Primary Designated Emergency Room:
Bayhealth Hospital, Kent Campus (Kent General)
Address: 640 S. State St., Dover, DE 19901
Phone: (302) 674-4700
Reporting Requirement: If an active duty member is admitted to or treated at a civilian emergency department, notify the Primary Care Manager (PCM) / Flight Medicine and the workplace supervisor within 24 hours to ensure authorization and documentation.

Outpatient Clinic Procedures (436th Medical Group)
Location: Building 300, Tuskegee Blvd, Dover AFB
Routine & Occupational Care:
Appointment Line: Call (302) 730-4633
Occupational Health / Bioenvironmental / Public Health: Coordinates annual medical surveillance, audiograms, respirator clearances, and fetal protection program restrictions

Non-Emergency After-Hours:
Call the MHS Nurse Advice Line at 1-800-TRICARE (874-2273) prior to seeking off-base urgent care to avoid unauthorized medical billing

meta.shelterInPlace:
1.	Alert all personnel to move to the Shelter-in-Place (SIP) location. ROOM #3
2.	Turn HVAC system off. LOCATED: MAIN BREAK AREA, TO THE RIGHT OF ENTRANCE TO ROOM 3
3.	Open SIP Kit (if applicable), begin running checklist. (Highest Ranking individual should take the lead).
4.	Secure all SIP room doors, ensuring they are secured and locked.
5.	(Optional) Wet towels from SIP kit and place towels firmly under the doors.
6.	Seal off doors, ventilation systems and windows using pre-cut plastic and duct tape from SIP kit. Ensure tape is fully connected around all edges of pre-cut plastic.
7.	Take accountability using recall roster in your SIP kit.
8.	Call your Unit Control Center (UCC) to report your building number and accountability.
9.	WAIT….do not leave SIP room until given the “ALL CLEAR”.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
Inside the Immediate Incident Area 

AVOID
•	If an escape route is accessible, evacuate the immediate area. Leave your belongings behind.
•	Evacuate even if others will not agree to follow you. Help others evacuate, if possible. Prevent others from entering the area.
•	Call 911 when you are safe.
•	Stay on the phone until the operator ends the call.
•	Follow any law enforcement instructions.
•	If in view of or approaching law enforcement personnel, keep your hands visible.
•	Do not attempt to move wounded individuals.

DENY
•	If evacuation is not possible, find a place to create a barricade between you and the active shooter.
•	Barricade where you are less likely to be found by the active shooter, provide you protection, and not restrict your options for movement.
•	If possible, lock the door and/or block the door with heavy furniture. Turn off any lights and cover windows.
•	Remain quiet and silence any devices (e.g., a cell phone) that may give away your location.
•	If safe to do so, call 911 (Stay on the phone until the operator ends the call).

DEFEND
•	As a last resort, and only when your life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt and/or incapacitate the shooter.
•	  Personnel should use whatever means possible to overpower the subject to save further lives.
•	Use the minimum force necessary to subdue the shooter, however, deadly force is authorized when an individual. reasonably believes they or others in the area are in immediate danger of death or serious bodily harm.

Information to Provide to Law Enforcement or 911
•	Number of active shooters, if more than one.
•	Location of the shooter(s).
•	Physical description of shooter(s).
•	Time you observed the shooter(s).
•	Number and type of weapons held by the shooter(s).
•	Number of potential victims at the location.

When Law Enforcement Arrives
•	Law enforcement’s purpose is to stop the active shooter as soon as possible.
•	Officers will proceed directly to the area in which the last shots were heard and will not stop to help injured persons until the shooter is neutralized.
•	Remain calm and follow instructions.
•	Place any items in your hands on the ground.
•	Immediately raise your hands and spread your fingers.
•	Always keep hands visible.
•	Do not impede law enforcement officers’ movements, such as holding on to them for safety.
•	Provide any information that may assist them in countering the threat.
•	Avoid pointing, screaming, and/or yelling.
•	Do not stop to ask officers for help or directions when evacuating, just proceed in the direction they instruct you to go.
•	Move quickly to the assembly point.
•	Expect to stay at the assembly point until the situation is under control.
•	Know that you might be interviewed by law enforcement.
•	Do not leave the assembly point until instructed by law enforcement.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter:
WINDS/TORNADO
1.	Supervisors notify personnel of weather conditions.
2.	If there is a watch, direct securing / sheltering of outside equipment / material if time permits.
3.	If there is a warning notify personnel to take immediate cover. ROOM #_3_______
Examples:
a.	Lowest lever, and most interior room.
b.	Inside hallway at the lowest level of the building.
c.	Under a piece of sturdy furniture such as a workbench, heavy table, or desk.
d.	If outdoors, get inside building or shelter if possible. If there is no time to get indoors, lie in a ditch or low-lying area and use your arms to protect the head and neck.
4.	If possible, monitor local radio / television stations for current information.
5.	Do not leave the facility until given the “ALL CLEAR”. 
6.	Up-channel information through the chain-of-command; call your Unit Control Center to report injuries and building damage.

EARTHQUAKE

1.	If inside, stay inside and crawl under a desk or get next to a solid or bulky object, curl up into a fetal position and stay put until the shaking stops and you are sure it is safe to exit.
2.	Stay away from glass, windows, outside doors and walls, and anything that could fall such as lighting fixtures or furniture.
3.	After the shaking stops, supervisors help evacuate the building, turning off utilities where possible, and secure classified material.
4.	Once outside, get to an open area away from buildings or unstable objects. If possible, go to the designated rally point. If outside during an earthquake, remain outside and locate to an open area.
5.	Once personnel have cleared the building, do not allow anyone to re-enter damaged buildings.
6.	Supervisors conduct accountability of personnel and report personnel status to your Unit Control Center.
7.	Perform first aid (if needed).

the wall next to the utility sink. The utility sink is to the left of the washer and dryer.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
DAF Traffic Safety Program (DAFI 91-207): Train personnel on mandatory use of seat belts and helmets, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotters while backing, vehicle training requirements, and restrictions on electronic device use while operating vehicles on- or off-base.
Seat Belts / Occupant Restraints: All persons operating or riding in motor vehicles must wear installed restraint systems as prescribed by the manufacturer. Drivers are responsible for ensuring all passengers are briefed on and use required restraints.
Motorcycle / ATV Training: Personnel must complete required safety training before riding a motorcycle, and local units should address required PPE, licensing, refresher training, and safety representative contacts.
Pedestrian / Bicycle Awareness: Emphasize local roadway crossing hazards, visibility
requirements, spotter use, and other pedestrian or bicycle precautions specific to the installation.

Local Traffic Hazards / Vehicle Notes:
Main Gate (Main / North Gate)  High-volume commercial and POV traffic. Heavy equipment transit is restricted during peak hours (0630-0830 and 1530-1730). Use caution when navigating barriers designed for Force Protection.
Commercial Gate (South Gate)  Primary entry point for construction deliveries and oversized loads. Watch for blind spots, slow-turning semi-trucks, and security check queues blocking the lane.
Airfield / Flightline Access Gates ✈  FOD (Foreign Object Damage) Hazards: Ensure tires are checked and cleared of stones or debris before entering airfield access points. Ground equipment must yield to all taxiing aircraft and emergency response vehicles.
Pavement Maintenance Zones ⚠  Transition zones between gravel yards and paved base roads.
Mud and debris tracked onto public base roads by heavy equipment must be cleared immediately to prevent motorcycle and vehicle slippage.

Vehicle Training & Documentation
To legally operate GMVs and specialized construction equipment, training must be explicitly tracked and documented:
AF Form 2293 (USAF Motor Vehicle Operator Identification Card): Must be carried by the operator, detailing every specific class of equipment they are authorized to operate (e.g., graders, loaders, dump trucks).
AF Form 483 (Flightline Driver's License): Must be in possession of any operator driving on the airfield flightline, complete with current annual flightline driver training certification

meta.documentNotes: AF Form 55 will be used to document safety, fire and health training unless other documentation is specified elsewhere. Documentation will be maintained by the supervisor within the work center and will contain the following minimum data: trainee name (last, first, middle initial), type of training and date of training. Neither the trainer or trainee signature is required unless specified in writing by the applicable chain of authority. The 14 mandatory items can be documented as one item, i.e., course code for JSTO mandatory training. Job specific items and any additional training identified in a BE survey will be documented individually, as appropriate.

selectedModules.title: Hazardous Energy Control
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 21; 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train authorized employees to recognize hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy present, and the methods and means for isolation and control. Train affected employees on the purpose and use of lockout/tagout procedures, and instruct all other employees on the prohibition against restarting locked or tagged equipment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document initial and refresher training when job assignments, machines, processes, or energy control procedures change, or when inspections show employee knowledge gaps.

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide local flight line driving rules, markings, vehicle lighting requirements, restricted areas, and aircraft hazard awareness before granting driving privileges.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use installation or unit-approved training and certification for airfield/fight line operations, to include local speed, spotter, and no-lone-zone requirements.
